title: Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández highlights tribal water rights bill and voter engagement efforts
text:
Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández highlights tribal water rights bill and voter engagement efforts
Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, currently serving in the U.S. Congress representing New Mexico’s 3rd district, addressed several key issues on her Twitter account on September 15, 2026.
In a tweet posted at 18:09 UTC, Leger Fernández announced legislative progress regarding water rights and infrastructure for Native communities. She wrote, "Agua es vida. Water is life and key to Tribal sovereignty. My bill passed committee today to help the Navajo Nation and Taos, Nambé, Pojoaque, San Ildefonso and Tesuque Pueblos recover lost settlement funds and build water infrastructure. It already passed the Senate thanks to https://t.co/WkZgP7uJ2S".
Later that day at 19:01 UTC, she marked National Voter Registration Day by encouraging civic participation among New Mexicans: "Today is National Voter Registration Day! Voting is your right and your voice. Take a few minutes today to check your voter registration, update your information if needed, and learn about upcoming election deadlines in New Mexico. Visit https://t.co/BcwHtGaqvp for up-to-date https://t.co/ohzlOQyTLa".
At 21:18 UTC on the same day, Leger Fernández commented on concerns about political corruption involving former President Donald Trump’s family: "Trump Jr.’s wedding is just the latest example of the Trump gold collar crimes and corruption. Foreign influences have poured millions into the pockets of the president and his family. What did they ask for in return? https://t.co/XsQT4DOQAf".
Leger Fernández has represented New Mexico’s 3rd District since replacing Ben Ray Luján in 2021, . She was born in Las Vegas, New Mexico in 1959 and resides in Santa Fe as of age 63. Her electoral history includes victories over Alexis Martinez Johnson in both the 2020 (58.7% to 41.3%) and 2022 (58.2% to 41.8%) general elections as well as defeating Sharon Clahchischilliage in the 2024 general election with a close margin (41.8% to 43.7%).
